Uranium.basis: Carborundum Buffalo Avenue complex (1801 Buffalo Ave): a location of the Manhattan Engineer District uranium-rod forming/coating/canning work (1943-44). EEOICPA-covered.

Carborundum Globar Plant: fabricated uranium rods for the Manhattan Engineer District (1943-44) and manufactured uranium, plutonium and carbide pellets + zirconium/hafnium/titanium for AEC reactor-materials programs (1959-67). EEOICPA-covered AWE/DOE facility.

Former Praxair / Union Carbide "15-Acre" site, adjacent to the ex-Electro Metallurgical (Electromet) plant on 47th St. Radioactive slag is interspersed in the surface soil/fill: naturally-occurring radioactive material enhanced by industrial processing (TENORM), primarily THORIUM and RADIUM (Th-232 and U-238/Ra-226 decay chains), tied to the Electromet uranium/thorium legacy — 1965-72 processing produced 505 tons of slag bearing 9,212 lb thorium dioxide + 1,293 lb U3O8 yellowcake, land-disposed at the Lake Ontario Ordnance Works. A MARSSIM gamma walkover survey (Ludlum NaI, Bicron) delineated the impacted-slag zones; gamma-spectroscopy of slag samples (EPA 901.1m) detected Radium-226, Radium-228, Actinium-228, Thallium-208, Thorium-234, Uranium-235 and Bismuth/Lead daughters. Source: Covanta/Praxair Remedial Investigation Report (LaBella, 2013).

Carborundum Globar Plant: fabricated uranium rods for the Manhattan Engineer District (1943-44) and manufactured uranium, plutonium and carbide pellets + zirconium/hafnium/titanium for AEC reactor-materials programs (1959-67). EEOICPA-covered AWE/DOE facility.
Carborundum Buffalo Avenue complex (Bldg 82/30/32): part of the Buffalo Avenue plant that performed Manhattan Engineer District uranium work. EEOICPA-covered.

Former Electro Metallurgical (Electromet) plant. Produced uranium metal from UF4 (green salt) for the Manhattan Project / AEC 1942-53, then processed uranium AND thorium commercially under NYS radioactive-material license 950-0139 — 1965-72 Union Carbide made 505 tons of slag bearing 9,212 lb thorium dioxide + 1,293 lb uranium oxide. Surface soil around Buildings 163/166 (and wall/floor seams of Bldg 163) carries gamma-emitting radionuclides above DOE guidelines in the thorium-232 and uranium-238 decay chains. Per the DOE FUSRAP Elimination Report, the U-238/Ra-226 ratio indicates NATURAL uranium — i.e. the contamination is TENORM from the licensed commercial operations, NOT the MED/AEC weapons work, so DOE eliminated the site from FUSRAP (no federal remedial authority).
